## Independent generation-result contract prepared for review — 2026-11-05

The investigator continues with a concrete result/provenance design after the source and public-dependency milestones. **This is a proposal, not an approved or implemented schema/API.** Existing local source commit `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`, accepted resources and all scientific evidence remain unchanged; the owner worktree is clean.

Recommended first slice: save/read an **already completed GenerationTrace** in one uncompressed NumPy NPZ artifact with a JSON manifest. Preserve the five native arrays byte-for-byte (dtype/shape/values), original zeros, projected strings, occurrence/return permutation, duplicate rows, seed, native return/descriptor values and explicit provenance unknowns. Separate the original scientific producer from a later exporter/reader. Native AMP/MIC scores keep their current meanings; no measured MIC, calibration, chemistry or biological claim is added. Failed/interrupted generation is not serialized as a successful empty result.

Reuse NumPy storage, optional Recorda caller-owned journals/references and Ackredit's detached attribution APIs. Do not copy a generic recorder, resolver, bibliography service, molecular parser or PeptideMT receipt format. Saving/reading retained science creates no new generation or scientific credit. The descriptive method-profile need remains in existing #2. Analogue/posterior archives, live attribution, migration, CLI, feedback/training/family/target, release and contact stay separate.

Source inspection identifies a concrete implementation prerequisite: the current eager package initializer and `inference.translate_tokens` import Torch. A reader submodule alone cannot be model-backend-free. A future candidate needs a controlled lazy/light-vocabulary refactor preserving existing APIs and scientific projection behavior.

Evidence scope is explicit:
- A finite **NumPy 2.4.6 primitive** probe preserves six synthetic arrays' dtype/shape/element bytes, signed zeros, adjacent FP32/FP64 values and endianness with pickle disabled; no Torch, HydrAMP result/schema, neural call or learned read. Supervision: 1.69 s /61,755,392 bytes aggregate RSS (~59 MiB), CPU0/1/one thread.
- The initial combined Recorda/Ackredit probe **never starts** because the shared-host resource guard refuses it. A later reading below conservative retry-start headroom defers the retry. No combined integration pass or runtime adoption is claimed.
- Recorda source is `ff52fa5d8628d796f413b833c8abe73907990cf9` (0.3.3); inspected Ackredit editable source is `74f865d7eca1f5386235885d4ea001e53b5b822d`, installed metadata `0.12.0+11.g74f865d`, fifteen commits behind fetched main. No source/environment upgrade or public 0.12.1 qualification is inferred.

Concrete payload, failure behavior, ownership, bounds, proposed implementation order and acceptance are in consumer design source `devguide/hydramp_result_contract.md` (SHA-256 `ce32baaa65cdce9a6474f95bac3a65ec5425fd3601bbdeb8f6e8983f4f4ed70b`). Review receipt: `devguide/evidence/hydramp_result_contract_review.json`, SHA-256 `78a28d8956f2d9031a33f65f9047ce3a661e1fcc22e9b3df843728017cedc68d`. Raw evidence owned by #4/#2 / uibcdf/peptidemt#32; review 2026-11-19.

Investigator agreement on this new result/attribution contract precedes implementation under the existing readiness agreement. Routine resources remain delegated under D49. #4 stays open; no new source commit, push, package/model publication or external contact occurs.

## Additional consumer need from proposed saved-result contract — 2026-11-05

Related product proposal: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6673257407; consumer uibcdf/peptidemt#32. This extends the evidence for **this existing proposal**; it does not approve a new profile/API or change any scientific definition.

The proposed first saved-generation result needs an owner-controlled description of the meanings already implemented in local source commit `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`: original 0..20 vocabulary and all-zero omission, original-zero-token scoring, native occurrence/return order, explicit seed/unfiltered-one-attempt scope, raw AMP/MIC score meanings and actual selected descriptor settings. Preserve descriptor values already computed; neither export nor inspection calculates them.

Distinguish a selected backend/instance from a generic defaults catalogue. `LegacyModlampProperties.pi_amide` / `Modlamp433Properties.pi_amide` and `expected_version` are current class/instance settings, and custom property providers are accepted by the existing generator. Known selected settings may be described; unknown/custom settings remain explicit rather than assigned the selected profile's defaults. Descriptor method assumptions never establish molecular termini/chemistry.

Original scientific producer/source/resource identities must survive a later export by newer software; exporter/reader identity is separate. A pure-data profile reader must not load checkpoints/PCA, import optional descriptor engines, calculate properties or credit new science. Avoid a second consumer-authored parameter table. Tests of a future capability must check the description against actual delegated kwargs, preserve detached data and distinguish unknown/unverified provenance.

The concrete first result contract remains for investigator review in `devguide/hydramp_result_contract.md`; receipt `devguide/evidence/hydramp_result_contract_review.json` SHA-256 `78a28d8956f2d9031a33f65f9047ce3a661e1fcc22e9b3df843728017cedc68d`. No provider code, pin, accepted resource, model call, scientific acceptance or release changes; #2 remains open.

## Independent HydrAMP result/provenance contract prepared — 2026-11-05

Owner design: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6673257407; existing method-profile need: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/2.

The investigator's continuation commissions a **decision-ready proposal**, not a new approved result schema/API. First slice: retain/read completed generation traces with all five native arrays, original zero positions, strings/occurrences, native permutation/descriptor values and explicit history/unknowns. One uncompressed NumPy archive plus JSON manifest is recommended; scientific producer identity remains separate from later exporter/reader identity. No PeptideMT receipt refactor, molecular parser, score reinterpretation or selector/M1–M8 change is proposed.

Recorda keeps optional caller-owned recording/references and Ackredit keeps detached bibliography/contextual uses. Source review finds that a reader must first address the eager Torch import and vocabulary location, preserving existing APIs and original token projection. Actual implementation and optional-provider adoption require the stated regressions and readiness agreement.

A finite NumPy primitive probe passes on synthetic arrays (1.69 s /~59 MiB aggregate RSS); it is **not a HydrAMP format implementation or scientific result**. The combined provider probe never starts due to the shared-host guard and its retry remains deferred below conservative headroom. No combined integration pass, models/parameters, neural evaluation, GPU or public-release claim follows. Owner runtime/source/lock/environment and accepted resources remain unchanged.

Maintained proposal: `devguide/hydramp_result_contract.md`, SHA-256 `ce32baaa65cdce9a6474f95bac3a65ec5425fd3601bbdeb8f6e8983f4f4ed70b`. Receipt: `devguide/evidence/hydramp_result_contract_review.json`, SHA-256 `78a28d8956f2d9031a33f65f9047ce3a661e1fcc22e9b3df843728017cedc68d`. Native findings, failure behavior, format bounds, source/provider pins and acceptance are recorded; broader #32/#4/#2 remain open. No new commit, push, package/model publication, feedback, training, family/target or external contact occurs.

## Current result-contract review checkpoint — 2026-11-05

A concrete independent generation save/read proposal is ready for investigator review: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6673257407. It preserves the existing native arrays, token/string distinctions, occurrence mapping, scores/descriptor values and provenance unknowns, with original producer and later exporter identities kept separate. One NumPy archive is recommended; optional caller-owned Recorda references and detached Ackredit data retain their existing owners. Related descriptive profile work remains in #2.

The controlled NumPy storage primitive passes on synthetic arrays without Torch/models. The combined provider mechanism probe never starts because of the shared-host resource guard; no integration pass is claimed. The eager package/Torch import is a concrete implementation prerequisite. This is a proposal under the existing readiness agreement, not approval or implementation of a schema/API, a new scientific acceptance or execution. Current source commit remains `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`; runtime, locks and accepted resources are unchanged.

## Previous installation checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The unchanged private dev7 wheel installs with seventeen freshly downloaded, hash-verified public base/test dependency wheels in a new Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.14.7 environment. Native dependency checking passes for eighteen distributions; sixteen exports and seventeen guarded installed codec tests pass. No retained third-party payloads, learned reads or neural evaluations are used. Source remains local commit `a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`; its worktree is clean.

Exact scope, artifacts, limits and evidence: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6672939016. This qualifies the exact public locked dependency route with a private own wheel, not public HydrAMP distribution, a clean public build toolchain, optional modlAMP or other platforms. The next product task is a concrete independent result/provenance contract review, preserving Recorda/Ackredit ownership; no new schema/API or scientific acceptance is inferred.

## Previous source/package baseline checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The investigator-authorized local `peptidemt-product-baseline` branch contains commit **`a77baff9de97e8ab4ae101b9b0c79122dea22ce3`**, exactly matching reviewed tree `2476a08a50d32779db2f43683928450e62b66f91`. Its worktree is clean and all other branch references are preserved. This commit has not been pushed. Private dev7 consolidates the existing runtime/tests/documentation/lock and packaging presentation; all nine dev6 runtime modules and original reference remain unchanged.

Directory/source-archive builds produce byte-identical wheels; a fresh installed codec check passes seventeen tests with zero neural evaluations or learned-asset reads. Native dependency checking passes. This uses faithful retained local dependency payloads, not a clean public dependency-install route or all-platform qualification. Initial engineering failures are diagnosed and retained.

Exact artifacts, scope and evidence: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6672423144. The single local commit succeeds with native exit 0; prior preparation receipts remain unchanged. Git identity alone changes no package payloads, so the successful build/installed checks are reused. No push, release, new scientific acceptance or author contact follows. Independent result/workflow design and public distribution prerequisites remain open.

## Previous product-review checkpoint — 2026-11-05

Current local dev6 has nine matching source/wheel/installed modules and sixteen public exports. Encoder, analogue and codec capabilities now have separate evidence; exact dev3/D41 and dev5/D44 acceptance remain distinct. Current documentation/navigation is updated in the owner redesign worktree. No runtime code or artifact changes.

The core is an independent expert Python library in its pinned local CPU profile. Source is still uncommitted. Next: one coherent reproducible source/package baseline, build presentation/dependency-route qualification, then a reviewed independent result/workflow contract. CLI remains optional. No new acceptance, calls, training, release or contact follows.

Full current review and source/evidence identities: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/4#issuecomment-6671622876

## Original review commission and initial resource record (preserved)

## Purpose

Give the modern fork a systematic review as an independently usable scientific tool, rather than relying on its PeptideMT integration as proof of product readiness. Preserve the original reference and credit; this issue does not select a new public name or promise a release.

## Review scope and completion criteria

- Map supported and unsupported scientific operations, native AMP/MIC meanings, original token/string distinctions, descriptor definitions, unknown chemistry and failure behavior. Scope the modern inference port separately from unqualified training/analogue routes.
- Review standalone API/CLI usability, explicit configuration/seeds, occurrence identity, structured results, provenance and truthful diagnostics without requiring PeptideMT. Reuse existing owner tests; identify meaningful missing regressions rather than mechanically duplicating them.
- Assess reproducible CPU installation, actual dependency closure/origins, Python/dependency claims, startup/resource controls, offline operation and checkpoint/PCA acquisition. Exact local Python 3.14 execution is not all-platform support or a qualified public installer.
- Audit method/software attribution, original notices, versioning and data/model use boundaries; retain the unresolved starter-versus-original-Drive byte identity and broader redistribution/output-use questions.
- Prepare user documentation, a retained-data example, limitations/model card and a prioritized product backlog. Record observed defects in their owning issues. Machine-readable profile metadata already belongs to #2.
- Finish with an evidence-backed readiness assessment and explicit remaining blockers; packaging/release implementation and publication remain separately authorized actions.

Interest from original authors is a separate collaboration question; useful standalone modernization does not depend on creating a new algorithm.

Consumer tracking: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/32
Accepted current resource: experimental AMP generation under PeptideMT D41; provider `hydramp-torch==0.0.0.dev3`, wheel SHA-256 `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`. Evidence and preserved limits: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8#issuecomment-6618984173.

This is investigator-requested future work to retain and review, not authorization for a new experiment, training, GPU, package/model release or external publication. Current model-call budgets are exhausted. Preserve the original reference, exact bundles, declared chemistry and all existing FAIL diagnostics.
